# Agents and Harnesses

- **An agent** is the autonomous actor — the thing that reasons, plans, uses tools, remembers, and pursues goals over multiple steps.
- **A harness** is the runtime / scaffolding that turns a raw language model into a working agent.
  - _**The harness** is the engine and chassis. **The agent** is the driver + the behavior that emerges once the model is running inside that chassis._


## Agent Harness Diagram
![Agent Harness Diagram](/assets/images/agent-harness-diagram.png "Agent Harness Diagram")



### More precise breakdown

| Concept | What it is | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Model** | The raw intelligence (weights) | Qwen, DeepSeek, Claude, Llama, Ajax (abliterated), etc. |
| **Harness** | The runtime that gives the model a loop, tools, memory, sandboxes, skills, messaging, persistence, etc. | Hermes, OpenClaw, goose, OpenHands, OpenCode, Agent Zero |
| **Agent** | The resulting autonomous system that actually does work | Copilot, OpenCode, Agent Zero |

**The harness determines:**
- How long the agent can run
- Whether it has persistent memory and can create its own skills
- What tools (MCP servers) it can reach
- Whether it lives in messaging apps, a terminal, a web UI, or a full Linux desktop
- How isolated / sandboxed its actions are
- How easy it is to observe, interrupt, or improve it

A good harness {Hermes, OPenCode, Agent Zero, OpenClaw, goose, etc.} dramatically changes what kind of agent you can actually have. A weak or missing harness leaves you with just a chatbot that forgets everything between messages

A harness is the runtime that gives a model a loop, tools, memory, and an
environment in which to act. It determines how long an agent can run, what it
can access, and how its work can be observed and controlled.

## Agentic development environments

An [{{< glossary "(ADE) Agentic Development Environment" popup="hover" >}}](https://davidgeeraerts.github.io/AI/appendices/glossary.html#ade-agentic-development-environment) runs, supervises, and orchestrates several coding agents in parallel. Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode stay the agents. The ADE gives each task a session, often its own git worktree, and a terminal or desktop pane where you watch it. [{{< glossary "Agent orchestration" popup="hover" >}}](https://davidgeeraerts.github.io/AI/appendices/glossary.html#agent-orchestration) here means that supervision. It is the same category of app, not an agent SDK and not the editor you type in.

[SpyNEL](https://github.com/agent0ai/spynel), already named below, drives Codex, Claude Code, and other harnesses from one chat (and from Telegram or WhatsApp). Its README does not describe per-task worktrees, so it is not a row in this table.

Cells were checked against each project's repository or docs in November 2026. These apps do not ship a model. The agent you attach does.

## Supporting infrastructure

- **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** connects agents to tools and services.
- Sandboxed execution environments such as Docker, Daytona, Modal, E2B, and
  browser infrastructure help isolate agent actions.
- Persistent memory and agent-written skills support longer-running work.
- **SpyNEL** orchestrates existing coding harnesses. See [Agentic development environments](#agentic-development-environments) for the parallel-workspace apps.
- **DOX / AGENTS.md** hierarchies give agents maintainable project context.




## [agents.md](https://agents.md/)


#### Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?
[Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful...](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988)

Repository context files can affect coding-agent performance [@gloaguen2026agentsmd].

| Condition | Effect on success rate | Effect on cost / steps |
|---|---|---|
| LLM-generated context files | Slightly worse on average (~ –0.5% on SWE-bench Lite, ~ –2% to –3% on the new bench; negative in most configs) | +20–23% inference cost; +2.5–4 extra steps per task |
| Human-written context files | Modest average gain (~ +4% on the developer-file benchmark) | Still + up to ~19% cost / more steps |
| Overall | “Does not generally improve task success rates” | Clear, consistent cost increase |


Practical takeaway that matches the evidence: Keep any AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md extremely short. Prefer only non-discoverable facts (exact test/build commands that differ from the obvious, hard “never touch X”, unusual tooling). Long files that restate what is already in the code, README, or package.json are the ones most likely to waste tokens for little or no gain.



## Enterprise-level agentic engineering

### [Kortix CompanyOS](https://kortix.com/)
> is an open-source, cloud-native agent harness designed to run a company’s work as code.
> Kortix sits above personal coding or messaging agents. It is the operating system layer for teams that want agents doing real, ongoing company work (sales, support, engineering triage, marketing loops, ops, etc.) while keeping configuration, memory, and outcomes reviewable, versioned, and human-gated.

| Aspect | Kortix CompanyOS | Personal harnesses |
|---|---|---|
| Core idea | Company as code; agents + skills + memory in one git repo | Personal agent that lives with you (messaging, coding, memory) |
| Scale | Team / organization, swarms, event-driven | Individual or small-team |
| Governance | Change requests, permissions-as-code, agent principals | Lighter or tool-level permissions |
| State | Shared company memory + per-session computers | Per-user curated memory + skills |
| Best fit | Internal tooling, ops, multi-agent company workflows | Daily personal leverage, coding, always-on assistant |
